pass_a_gloss: Tome 4. Vision of Egypt. [Lemma, Isaiah 19:1:] Behold, the Lord sits on a light cloud, and will come into Egypt, and the handmade things of Egypt will be shaken from before his face, and their heart will be defeated in them. In what way indeed the country of the Egyptians has been saved and netted toward piety, through faith clearly that in Christ, although being of many gods and sick with error beyond place, the prophet tries to teach in these [words]. For they were as in deep darkness, having wholly not known the God by nature and truly being maker and Lord of all, and fastening reverence to the creation; and what is still more unreasonable than this, being shown craftsmen of their own gods, and having a many-shaped swarm of idols in the precincts, so as also to mould types of irrational animals, and, setting up altars, to sacrifice to them. It was needed then, sin abounding among them, that grace should super-abound, and that the physician should shine upon those so hatefully sick, and that upon those darkened in heart the divine and heavenly light should flash. Behold then, he says, the Lord sits on a light cloud, and will come into Egypt. But what would it wish to indicate, that the Lord is seen upon a light cloud? Come, let us say as is possible. Some of the interpreters said the light cloud is the holy flesh of the Lord, that is, the temple taken from the Virgin; and they liken it to a cloud because of its being freed perhaps from the more earthy movements and desires, up and as it were on high. For truly all-pure and freed from all earthy uncleanness is the holy body of the Saviour of us all, Christ. And others again have supposed that the holy Virgin has been named light cloud. And I for my part think that perhaps to say that he sits on a light cloud also signifies to us a breadth of other thoughts. For in many ways the blessed prophets, beholding the glory of God, have written the visions. For Isaiah says he has beheld the Lord Sabaoth on a throne high and lifted up, the highest rational powers standing around in a circle, both hymning him and saying that heaven and earth are full of his glory. And the all-wise Daniel seats an Ancient of days on a throne; and he maintains that thousand thousands minister to him, and says myriad myriads stand around; and that he has beheld also as a Son of Man [the section breaks off].

lemmas.gloss: has been drawn as in a net

pass_b_english: “Behold, the Lord is seated on a light cloud, and he will come to Egypt, and the handmade things of Egypt will be shaken before his face, and their heart will be overcome within them” (Isaiah 19:1).

In these words the prophet sets out to teach how the land of the Egyptians was saved and drawn as in a net into true religion, plainly through faith in Christ, although it worshipped many gods and was sick with error beyond measure.

For they were, as it were, in deep darkness. They knew nothing at all of him who is God by nature and truly the Maker and Lord of all, and they fastened their worship on the creation. What was still more absurd, they made themselves the craftsmen of their own gods and kept a swarm of idols of every shape in their temples, so that they even moulded likenesses of irrational animals, set up altars, and sacrificed to them.

Since sin had multiplied among them, grace had to abound all the more (Romans 5:20); the Physician had to shine upon those so grievously sick, and the divine and heavenly light had to flash upon those darkened in heart.
“Behold, then,” he says, “the Lord is seated on a light cloud, and he will come to Egypt.” But what might it mean that the Lord is seen on a light cloud? Come, let us say what we can.

Some interpreters have said that the light cloud is the holy flesh of the Lord, that is, the temple taken from the Virgin. They liken it to a cloud because it is free, perhaps, of the more earthly impulses and desires, and is, as it were, above and on high. For the holy body of Christ, the Saviour of us all, is truly all-pure and free of every earthly impurity. Others again have taken the holy Virgin to be what is called a light cloud.

For my part, I think that saying he sits on a light cloud may also hint to us at a breadth of other meanings. For the blessed prophets, when they beheld the glory of God, wrote down their visions in many ways. Isaiah says that he saw the Lord of hosts on a throne, high and lifted up, with the highest rational powers standing in a circle around him, singing his praise and saying that heaven and earth are full of his glory (Isaiah 6:1–3).

The all-wise Daniel seats the Ancient of Days on a throne; he insists that a thousand thousands serve him, and says that ten thousand times ten thousand stand around him (Daniel 7:9–10); and that he also saw one like a Son of Man…

choices.why: Gospel image of the net (compare Matthew 13:47) for the gathering of Egypt into faith.
εὐσέβεια here is right worship of God set against Egypt's many gods.
Christ as physician of the sick nation; capitalised because it names Christ.

choices.english: the temple taken from the Virgin
choices.why: Cyril's usual name for the Lord's body; the temple image is kept.
rejected: the body born of the Virgin

choices.why: δυνάμεις λογικαί are the angelic powers endowed with reason.
